intro:
Six channels, each with a codename. The codename is the point: in the field you say "go to Birch" and everyone turns one knob, which is the only channel plan that survives cold hands and a bad signal. Write the two you are using on tape on the back of each radio.

They are grouped by the radio your group actually has, not by band. Cedar and Birch are 2 m and Flint and Quartz are 70 cm — both work on every dual-band handheld ever sold, from a Yaesu down to a twenty-dollar Baofeng. Gorse and Thistle are FRS, the bubble-pack sets sold in every outdoor shop, which need nothing set up but a channel number. Pick one group and stay in it. A DCS code is set on the amateur channels so your squelch stays shut unless it is one of your own radios — it is not encryption, and anyone scanning still hears you.
introz:
六个频率，每个都有一个代号。代号才是重点：在野外你只需要说「切到白桦」，所有人拧一下旋钮就行——在手冻僵、信号又差的时候，只有这种方案撑得住。把正在用的两个频率写在胶带上，贴到每台电台背面。

分组的依据是你的队伍实际拿着什么机器，而不是波段。雪松和白桦在 2 米波段，燧石和石英在 70 厘米波段——这两段所有双段手台都支持，从八重洲到一百多块的宝锋都能收发。金雀花和蓟草在 FRS 频段，就是户外店里卖的那种民用对讲机，除了选个信道之外什么都不用设。选定一组就别换。业余频段那几个都设了 DCS 码，这样只有自己人的电台才能打开静噪——但它不是加密，任何在扫频的人照样能听到你们。

stations.n: Cedar · open country, ridge to ridge
stations.z: 雪松 · 开阔地与山脊通联
stations.a: Open country — 2 m, on any dual-band handheld
stations.d: Your main channel outdoors. 2 m carries further over open ground and through trees than anything else your radio can transmit on, which is why this is the hiking, climbing and backcountry choice. It sits in the 146.400–146.580 MHz simplex block, far enough from the 146.520 calling frequency to stay out of the way.
stations.dz: 户外时的主频。在开阔地和林间，2 米波段的传播距离超过你这台电台能发射的任何其他频段，所以徒步、攀登和荒野活动都选它。它位于 146.400–146.580 MHz 直通段内，离 146.520 呼叫频率足够远，不会碍事。

stations.a: Open country — 2 m, on any dual-band handheld
stations.d: Same band, same DCS code, so moving here needs no discussion and no reprogramming. Agree the rule before you split up: if you lose each other on Cedar, go to Birch, and if that fails go back to Cedar and call every five minutes.
stations.dz: 同一波段、同一个 DCS 码，所以切过来不需要商量，也不需要重新设置。分头行动前先约定好规则：在雪松上失联就切到白桦，白桦也不行就回到雪松，每五分钟呼叫一次。

stations.z: 燧石 · 楼宇、停车场与场馆
stations.a: Town and indoors — 70 cm, on any dual-band handheld
stations.d: Indoors and downtown, swap to this. UHF gets through walls and bounces around street canyons far better than 2 m, so it wins in a concrete car park, a conference hall or a stadium. Out in open country it loses to Cedar, so this is a swap rather than an upgrade.
stations.dz: 在室内和市中心就切到这里。UHF 穿墙、在街道峡谷里反射的能力都远好于 2 米，所以在混凝土停车场、会场或体育馆里它占优。但在开阔的野外它不如雪松——这是场景切换，不是升级。

stations.a: Town and indoors — 70 cm, on any dual-band handheld
stations.d: Worth having in a city, where 70 cm is busier than the band plan suggests.
stations.dz: 在城市里值得存一个，因为 70 厘米的实际占用比频段规划看起来要热闹。

stations.n: Gorse · family, and anyone on a cheap radio
stations.z: 金雀花 · 家人，以及用便宜对讲机的人
stations.a: Anyone's radio — FRS, on any bubble-pack set
stations.d: FRS Channel 1. Nothing to set up beyond a channel number, and the radios are sold in every outdoor and hardware shop for the price of a meal — which makes this the realistic way to put children, partners and borrowed hands on the air. Expect a few hundred metres in town and a couple of kilometres with a clear line of sight. Note that 462 MHz is outside the VX-6R's transmit range: buy a pair of FRS sets for the group and let the VX-6 listen.
stations.dz: FRS 1 频道。除了选个信道之外什么都不用设，电台在任何户外店和五金店都买得到，价格跟一顿饭差不多——所以这是让孩子、家人和临时帮手上台最现实的办法。城里能通几百米，视野开阔时两三公里。注意 462 MHz 不在 VX-6R 的发射范围内：给队伍买一对 FRS 电台，VX-6 只负责收听。

stations.n: Thistle · a convoy on the road
stations.a: Anyone's radio — FRS, on any bubble-pack set
stations.d: FRS Channel 3. Two cars on a long drive is the case FRS handles best: you are within a kilometre of each other for hours, and the alternative is a phone call nobody should be making. Staying off Channel 1 matters here, because Channel 1 is the factory default and every other group on the highway is sitting on it.
stations.dz: FRS 3 频道。长途自驾的两辆车是 FRS 最合适的场景：连续几小时彼此都在一公里内，而替代方案是一个本来就不该打的电话。这里避开 1 频道很重要——1 频道是出厂默认值，高速上其他所有队伍都挤在上面。
